Subject: Recap: Eval scope & RPS / concurrency checklist

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the evaluation scheduled and scope locked. Please confirm the numbers below or correct them inline.

Success criteria (customer-provided):
- 95th pctl latency for 1,024-token generations <= 350ms under steady-state.
- End-to-end throughput target: sustain 150 RPS for API surface used by agents.
- No functional regressions vs your current inference outputs (we'll use your blind test set).

Workload & traffic profile (from today's discovery):
- Steady-state (expected): 150 RPS daytime, 30 RPS overnight.
- Peak/burst: short bursts to ~750 RPS for 20s every ~15 minutes (spiky agent warmups).
- Concurrency target: ~60 concurrent requests during peak; typical concurrency ~12.
- Token lengths: input tokens median ~80, 90th ~450; generation length median ~120, 90th ~1,024.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: ~40% streaming (partial tokens), 60% standard responses.
- Embedding/other endpoints: ~8% of requests are embeddings (~768-d vectors).

Attachments: I attached a blank ramp sheet (lumina-ramp-sheet.csv) and a small sample queries file (lumina-sample-queries.txt) for you to fill in tokens and percent distributions.

Proposed evaluation timeline and owners:
- Oct 15: Lumina returns completed ramp sheet + sample queries (owner: Olivia).
- Oct 18: Redwood to confirm VM/GPU configuration and test harness (owner: Aditya).
- Oct 20–27: 1-week evaluation window (controlled traffic from Lumina).
- Oct 28: Readout + success signoff (owners: Hannah / Olivia).

Open questions / asks for you:
1) Can you confirm whether the 750 RPS bursts are synthetic (replay) or real user-driven?
2) Please populate the sample queries file with a representative 50-query subset and indicate token counts.
3) Do you require data residency constraints for log retention during the POC?

Next steps: if that timeline works, Olivia, can you confirm by EOD Monday and upload the two attachments to the Drive link? Once we have the sheet, Aditya will map the traffic into a test harness and confirm expected slot sizing.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications below and we'll upload the files by Oct 15.

Clarifications:
- Bursts: these are real user-driven spikes tied to scheduled data-sync jobs (not synthetic). They happen after each sync window and last ~15–30s; 750 RPS is an upper bound, more commonly ~500 RPS.
- Token breakdown: we ran a quick histogram — median input 70, 90th 380; generation median 110, 90th 900. We'll populate exact counts in the sample file.
- Data residency: logs can be stored in US for the POC. We have no EU residency requirement for this trial.

One ask: can Redwood run the POC with a 500 RPS synthetic burst first and then we'll flip to real traffic for a final 48-hour stretch? We want to avoid impacting production while we iterate.

I'll upload the two files to the Drive folder by Oct 15 and leave a short README with the sample set choices.

Thanks for the updates — good notes. Technical quick-take on feasibility and recommended config: 

Feasibility:
- Sustaining 150 RPS steady-state with median token lengths you indicated is straightforward on our Dedicated trial nodes.
- Short bursts to 500–750 RPS are the risky part; handling 750 reliably for repeated bursts will likely need temporary burst capacity (extra worker pool) or rate-based throttling fallback.

Recommendations (short):
- Start with 500 RPS synthetic bursts for the initial run (this matches Olivia's ask). If stable, we can enable a transient GPU buffer to absorb 750 bursts for the final 48h.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated conversational prompts — should cut token compute by ~15–25% depending on overlap.
- Use batching window of 5–10ms for steady-state; aggressive batching for embeddings requests.
- For streaming requests, we recommend keeping max chunk size at 64 tokens to reduce tail latency variability.

Action items for engineering:
- Hannah: confirm test harness runbook and whether Lumina will route traffic through our staging endpoint or replay from logs.
- Karthik / me: we'll draft a sizing note (GPUs, pooling) and a fallback policy (throttle to 300 RPS) by Oct 18.

I'll attach a short sizing memo to the shared Drive once the sample queries are live.

- Aditya
